howDoI.q: How do I let my hero jump over a wall?
How do I add coins and a score?
How do I put a friendly monster in my game?
How do I make something that hurts a little?
How do I make a door that needs a key?
How do I join my levels into one game?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Your First Game is a Starter, and the last one: a small, whole game that uses a little of what the other Starters teach. It has a title, three short levels with signs in them, and an ending. It takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe). It is made to be copied and changed, and the Make it yours page at the end is a step-by-step guide to doing that.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Up and Down climb a ladder. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Spikes take a few hit points, once. A gumdrop is friendly. A key opens a locked door and is used up.

pages.head: Level 1: Walk and Jump
pages.html:
Level 1: Walk and Jump

The ARROWS WALK. SPACE JUMPS. sign comes first. A short way on, three coins, and then a brick wall two blocks high. The HOLD AN ARROW AND TAP SPACE sign says how to get over it. Beyond is a grassy hill with five coins on top, and a mint green gumdrop walking back and forth. The A GUMDROP IS FRIENDLY sign says to touch it: it pops, and Neka gets 50 points.

There are eight coins, ten points each, and the gumdrop's fifty, so a perfect level 1 is 130 points.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The walking and the jump. Open hero.chr in the character editor. The Left and Right arrows each start a walking sequence, and Space starts the jump. Gravity does the rest. The First Steps Starter explains these.
  • The wall and the hill. Open one.map in the map editor. The wall is four brick blocks. The hill is a row of grass over dirt. Both are solid, which is why Neka has to jump.
  • The coins. Open first.bbl in the blocks editor and pick coin. Its Score is 10 and Becomes block is sky, so a coin is gone once it is touched. The Coins and Score Starter goes further.
  • The gumdrop. Open first.mon in the monsters editor and pick the first monster. It walks four blocks and turns around. Its Power is 1, and a monster with a power under 100 is gone when it is touched. Its pictures are in first.mbl, where the block's Score is 50. The Meet the Monsters Starter explains it.
  • The signs. Each sign is a few ordinary blocks side by side with words drawn on them. Open one in the blocks editor and change the words.

pages.head: Level 2: Key and Door
pages.html:
Level 2: Key and Door

The SPIKES HURT. JUMP OVER THEM. sign stands before a single spike. Walk into it and it stings: Neka shows her hurt pose and has 40 hit points left. The spike then lies flat. Two more spikes follow, and this time a jump takes Neka over them.

Then a ladder leads up to a ledge with three coins and a key. The LOCKED. A KEY OPENS THE DOOR. sign stands under the ledge, by the locked door in a brick wall. Go up, take the key, come back and walk into the door. It opens and the key is used up. Five more coins lie beyond, then the exit.

Eight coins and a key: 105 points.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The spikes. In first.bbl pick spikeUp. Its Hit points is −10, and Becomes block is spikeFlat, so a spike hurts once and then lies down. Neka starts with 50 hit points: open hero.chr and look at the first counter. The Watch Your Step and Health and Hearts Starters go further.
  • The key. Pick key. On its Touch tab, Effect counter is counter 20 and Effect amount is 1, and Becomes block is sky.
  • The locked door. The gate block is solid. Its Effect counter is also counter 20, but its Effect amount is −1. A counter from 20 up will not go to zero or less, so with no key the touch does nothing and the door stays shut. With a key the touch pays one and the door turns into sky. The Keys and Doors Starter has the whole story.
  • No way around. The door is one block high, with an arch you walk under, and a wall of brick goes from there to the top of the level. Open two.map to see it.
  • The ladder. A column of ladder blocks. Up and Down climb it. First Steps explains ladders.

pages.head: Level 3: All Together
pages.html:
Level 3: All Together

The last level has a little of everything. Two spikes to jump over, three coins, a gumdrop to pop, a brick wall to jump, a key lying on the ground, and a locked door with three more coins and the exit behind it. The KEY FIRST, THEN THE DOOR sign says what to do.

Six coins, a key and a gumdrop: 135 points. Then the ending.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • The same blocks again. This level loads three.map but the same first.bbl, first.mon and hero.chr as the others. That is what makes the game one game: a level is just a map that uses the blocks and monsters you already made.
  • The order of things. Nothing here is new, only put in a different order: spikes, coins, gumdrop, wall, key, door. Move one in three.map and play to see what changes.
  • The ending. Open first.gam in the scene editor. Each level is a scene, and the door at its end is a link to the next scene. The last door links to the ending scene, which shows the won pictures and words.
  • The title and the demo. Scene 0 is the title, with its menu, story, how to play and credits pages, and a demo that plays when nobody touches a key.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

A small game is small partly because of what the engine does not have:

  • A level cannot be won by collecting everything: the exit door is always open. Doors need a key, but nothing needs a score.
  • A door cannot count coins. It can count a counter like keys, which is why the key is a counter.
  • Score cannot give a life at a number of points. Only a block with an effect can.
  • Neka cannot throw a star in this game. Game-Maker can do it, but it takes a few more pieces: the Throw It Starter shows how.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Open the game with Edit a copy, so the original stays safe. Then make one change at a time, and play after each. Each step says which Starter teaches that piece in full.

  1. Change the words. Open first.bbl in the blocks editor, pick a sign block (they are named like walk.sign) and change its words. Say something about your own game.
  2. Move a coin. Open one.map in the map editor and pick the coin block. Paint a trail of coins up the hill, or take the hill away. (Coins and Score)
  3. Make the wall taller. Paint another row of brick on the wall. Can Neka still jump it? How tall is too tall? (First Steps)
  4. Add a gumdrop. Paint another one in two.map. Change how far it walks in first.mon. (Meet the Monsters)
  5. Make spikes hurt more. Change spikeUp’s Hit points to −25. How many can Neka take now? (Health and Hearts, Watch Your Step)
  6. Move the key. Put it somewhere harder to reach in two.map. Put a ledge under it. (Keys and Doors)
  7. Add a power. A star or a pair of sneakers can make a hard jump possible. (Power Up)
  8. Add a talking friend. This game talks only with signs, to stay small. A friend who talks needs a few more pieces: a block for the friend, a scene for the talk and a link back to the level. The Say Something Starter has all three, ready to copy.
  9. Add a clock. A gate that shuts after a few seconds. (Beat the Clock)
  10. Draw your own hero. Open hero.cbl in the blocks editor and redraw her. She is two blocks tall.
  11. Add a level. Copy three.map to a new map, paint your own, and add a scene for it that links from level 3's door. (Room to Room)
  12. Change the song. Open first.cmf in the music editor and change a few notes.

When you have a game you like, use Export on the home page to play it as a DOS game or on a web page.
